chunks: Humayd, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Aban, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who assigns upon another man with dirhams, can he retract against him? He (peace be upon him) said: He cannot retract against him ever, except if he had become bankrupt before that.
ai.seo_question: Can a creditor retract a debt assignment in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the irrevocability of debt assignment (hiyal) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the original debtor remains bound to the assignee unless the debtor's insolvency (iflas) occurred prior to the transaction. It highlights the importance of verifying the debtor's financial status at the time of assignment to ensure the validity of the transfer. The ruling underscores the principle of finality in commercial contracts, preventing arbitrary retraction once the assignment is complete.
